physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the diaphragm, the broad sheet of muscle slung between the chest and the belly, the thing that pumps the breath if you let it and grips it if you do not. It is fitting. This is the code of provocation and release, and the diaphragm is where provocation lands first. A tone goes in the ear and the diaphragm catches before the mind catches. The breath stops on a held thought and the diaphragm holds it. The whole long argument the card is having lives there.

The shadow has its bodily floor in that grip. Years of half-spoken fear gather along the underside of the ribs, a quiet tightness no one quite names. The breath climbs out of the belly and gets shallow, lodging up near the collarbones, and the energy that should have stayed low and steady gets stuck behind the held breath. What looks like a personality, taut, easily set off, is closer to a muscle that has forgotten how to drop.

The climb out is also bodily. Breath returns to the belly the way it ran in a small child, low and unhurried, and the held thing softens of its own accord. Not by being talked out of. By being breathed through. The work runs in a band of muscle most people never feel.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the diaphragm, this code answers to Serine, an amino acid the body does make for itself, building it from what is already in the system rather than waiting for it to be brought in. Serine is one of the components the body uses to build the membranes of its cells, the thin walls that decide what crosses into the cell and what does not.

There is a teaching in that. This is the code of blockages and openings, of what passes through and what gets caught, and at its chemical floor it is built from the very stuff the body uses to make boundaries that breathe. A good membrane is not a wall. It is selective. It lets the right things in and the wrong things wait. The whole movement of the card, learning when to soften the grip and when to keep it, is the same teaching the body is already running at the scale of every cell.
